title: Aristotle: Justice, Constitutions, and Rule of Law

scenes.text: Why do citizens rebel and tear down their governments?
scenes.narration: Have you ever wondered why citizens overthrow their rulers? To find out, Aristotle studied one hundred fifty-eight constitutions to discover what makes a government stable and just.

scenes.text: Equal prizes for star players and benchwarmers cause resentment.
scenes.narration: Imagine an analogy from school sports. If the star player and someone who skipped practice receive the exact same award, both feel bitter. Aristotle called this proportionate equality: rewards should match your real contribution to society.

scenes.heading: Aristotle's Two Paths of Governance
scenes.narration: Here's how Aristotle sorted governments. When rulers serve the common public interest, you get normal regimes like monarchy or polity; but when rulers serve selfish greed, regimes become corrupt and unstable.

scenes.heading: Polity as the Golden Mean
scenes.narration: So, which practical system works best? Aristotle championed polity, rule by the middle class, because it avoids the arrogance of the wealthy and the ignorance of the poor, creating a stable golden mean.

scenes.quote: Law is a reason without Passion.
scenes.narration: While Plato wanted an all-powerful philosopher king, Aristotle placed his trust in the rule of law. Written laws carry collective wisdom across generations and remain fair because law is reason without passion.

scenes.heading: The Root Cause of Revolution
scenes.narration: Finally, notice what sparks revolutions. Aristotle warned that the main cause is psychological: whenever citizens feel treated unequally or unjustly, resentment turns into conspiracy, leading to regime change.

items: Distribute public honors according to proportionate equality
Middle class governance ensures the most stable polity
Rule of law guarantees reason without passion
scenes.narration: Remember these three big takeaways. Proportionate equality rewards societal merit, a large middle class guarantees political stability, and the rule of law replaces passion with reason.
